title: LUA-05..16 remain IN_PROGRESS: host API, capability, and limiter tests not yet written against real LuaJIT
symptom: 12 MUST requirements (LUA-05..16) are executable for the first time but unverified; their spec cases were never written because stub bindings made execution impossible.
root_cause: ISS-0153 stubs prevented any script from running, so no limiter or host-API behaviour could be observed. ISS-0161 removed that blocker but scoped itself to LUA-01..05.
acceptance_criteria: LUA-08/09/10 limiters proven to terminate scripts
notes: Filed per ISSUE_QUEUE.md forwarding rules rather than expanding ISS-0161's scope.
Motivating evidence: the first sandbox rule actually exercised under ISS-0161 (loadfile removal) turned out to be BROKEN. These 12 requirements have never been executed.

diagnosis.premise_correction: The issue's premise ('implemented but untested') is false. Execution against real LuaJIT shows 11 of the 12 requirements are not implemented, only partially implemented, or do not compile. Only LUA-14 is genuinely implemented-but-untested.
diagnosis.root_cause: src/lua/ is a Stage-8 scaffold written in May 2026 against bindings that could never execute. Every host_api register() discards ExecutionContext with `_ = context;` and registers a 0-upvalue closure, so no capability set is reachable at call time and NO capability check fires anywhere (verified: an empty CapabilitySet permits all 7 gated calls). The four state-touching host functions validate their arguments, discard them with `_ =`, and push nil. executeScript installs no instruction hook, no bounded allocator and no timeout, so instruction_limiter.zig / memory_limiter.zig / timeout.zig are dead code with no caller anywhere in src/. Two of those three files do not even compile (instruction_limiter.zig:39 discards lua_sethook's c_int; memory_limiter.zig:13 uses std.Thread.Mutex, removed in Zig 0.16) - invisible because src/lua_test_root.zig pins them with type-only references that force neither field-type resolution nor function-body analysis. Additionally loadSafeStdlib never calls luaopen_base, so pairs/pcall/error/type/setmetatable/_G are absent from any script run through executeScript, making stdlib.zig's load/loadstring/loadfile removals no-ops on that path and rendering realistic scripts unrunnable. This is the ISS-0155 anti-pattern at subsystem scale: correct names, correct signatures, correct error taxonomies and correct payload structs, all returning success without doing the work.
diagnosis.highest_severity_finding: LUA-06 is an absent security control, not a missing test: a Lua script today has unconditional access to every platform.* host function regardless of its declared manifest. ORCH should re-assess ISS-0169's MAJOR severity in light of this.
diagnosis.scope_recommendation: Recommend ORCH split into four sequential WF-03 runs: (1) LUA-05/06/07 context plumbing + capability enforcement + manifest, (2) LUA-08/09/10 limiters, (3) LUA-11/12/13 stateful host API, (4) LUA-14/15/16 time + events. Group 1 is a prerequisite for 3 and 4. The 12 specs define 169 test cases; CLAUDE.md caps a run at 4 requirements for exactly this blast-radius reason.
